Commentary.Commentary: So that is it! Sri Lanka finally get a win in the ODI series which also means they avoid the whitewash. South Africa on the other hand, will be disappointed that they could not finish the job after a wonderful platform. The cricketing action between the two sides does not end as there is one more ODI to go which will be played on the 12th of August at 2.30 PM local (9 AM GMT). Before that, you can also catch the action between England and India's second Test starting on the 9th of August. Take care and goodbye.

Sri Lankan captain, Angelo Mathews, says it was a very important victory and he is proud of the way his team performed. Mentions the two all-rounders played really well. Further adds it was a fantastic effort by the bowlers especially after the DLS method played into the hands of South Africa. Reckons there is improvement in the batting department and also credits the groundstaff for their effort and hard work.

Man of the Match, Dasun Shanaka, says there was no place for him before this game in the XI but grabbed his opportunity. Admits he was not nervous and he enjoyed his batting out in the middle. Ends by saying he is really happy with how the team performed.

South African captain, Quinton de Kock, says it is always difficult losing a game like this one. He adds it was a good match in the end though. Credits the character Sri Lanka showed. Admits they were still backing themselves when David Miller was out there. Ends by saying he enjoyed the responsibility as captain but is sad they could not finish on the winning side.

Akila Dananjaya then got rid of Amla and then in de Silva's one over, Klaasen and the well-set Duminy courtesy a run out took the long walk back. All of a sudden after that, run scoring got difficult. However, the visitors should have still chased this down especially after a handy cameo from Maharaj who fell on the last ball of the penultimate over, leaving the Proteas needing 8 in the last over with Miller on strike. But the southpaw's wicket on the second ball and Lakmal's excellent line and length in the last over gave Sri Lanka their narrowest win over the Proteas in ODIs. Earlier after being inserted on an overcast evening, a compact batting performance took Sri Lanka past 300 - what they failed to achieve in a full 50-over innings in over a year. It would have been a shame had rain robbed them off a victory tonight. Stay tuned for the presentation.

Hashim Amla and Quinton de Kock got them off to a flier before the left-hander perished. Then Reeza Hendricks walked out at no. 3 but did not stay out for long. Duminy though along with Amla, milked runs at ease and in no time the two added a 57-run stand. At that time, one would have felt, South Africa would chase this down in a canter but it wasn't to be.

Now where did it all change for the South Africans? The Duminy run out? Maybe. They were cruising before that. After the thumping their bowlers received at the hands of the Sri Lankan batsmen, their openers came out all guns blazing. Rain then intervened yet again, setting South Africa a revised target of 191 in 21 overs. Which was comparatively easier than the one they had to chase before (308).

Talk about snatching a defeat from the jaws of victory. Sri Lanka have done exactly that. What a nerve-wrecker. UFF! Credit to Suranga Lakmal, he kept his nerve, stayed as cool as possible and defended just 7 in the last over, also taking the wicket of David Miller. Outstanding!

Just the one and SRI LANKA WIN BY 3 RUNS! Excellent, excellent last over by Lakmal. Take a bow. He bowls it on a back of a length around middle, Dala mistimes it towards covers and gets to the other end. Smiles all around the Sri Lanka dressing room as they have finally beaten South Africa after 11 straight losses. Also, the last win over them came at this same venue in 2014.
A brace! Now 5 off the last ball! Short of a length on middle, Dala swings, he gets it off the inner half through square leg and the batsmen run two.
BEATEN! Lovely delivery! Bowls it closer to the batsman giving him no room. Dala tries to drive it straight down the ground but misses. 7 in 2 now.
A single! 7 from 3. Length ball on middle, Ngidi punches it down to long on and gets to the other end.
Lungi Ngidi walks out to the middle.

OUT! KABOOM! Miller is out of here and is that the game for Sri Lanka? Well they are surely favorites now. Lakmal, the experienced campaigner delivers. He bowls the slower delivery on a back of a length around off, Miller goes for the pull but gets an inside edge onto his stumps. The crowd erupts. Lakmal is all pumped up, Mathews is all pumped up. Sri Lanka now need one wicket to win. Whereas, South Africa need 8 from 4.
On the shorter side and outside off, Miller slaps it through covers and does not take a run. 8 from 5 now.
There is a long meeting going on between Lakmal and Mathews. They can't decide on the field they want. Finally they do and Lakmal now is ready to bowl.
Junior Dala is the next man in.

OUT! TIMBER! But is this wicket a little too late? Well, one would feel so as Maharaj walks back after playing a really good cameo. Thisara bowls it on a length around off, Maharaj swings but misses. The ball hits the top of off. 8 needed from the final over. David Miller on strike.

Direct hit needed... but missed. On a length around off, Miller taps it towards covers and sets off for a run. There is hesitation but they continue with the run. The fielder at point has a shy but misses. Replays though later on show Miller's dive would have saved him.

The batsman has played it to the point region. One run added to the total. Very smart by Maharaj, the last time he got a boundary, he played out two dots after that. This time he does the right thing by giving the strike over to Miller.
FOUR! Maharaj may have just slapped all the hopes away. On a length around off, Maharaj makes room and thrashes it past the diving cover fielder. A boundary and an important one.
Back of a length on off, Miller guides it towards point and gets to the other end.

NOT OUT! Maharaj again is in by quite a margin. He uses his feet and hits it down towards mid off. They go for a run. The fielder hits bull's eye at the non-striker's end. The ball deflects towards the mid-wicket region. There is an overthrow available but Miller does not want it. The umpire then signals for the third umpire and replays confirm Keshav is in.
Another direct hit at the bowler's end! Maharaj seems to be well in but just to be sure.
A single! Again Sri Lanka have Maharaj on strike. He taps this towards point and gets to the other end. How useful would it have been, had he done this on the ball before?
And again! This was even uglier than the last one. Outside off and it was the slower one. Maharaj was a week early into his shot and he misses it by a month. 2 dots in a row,
How needless is this? A boundary in the last ball, what should he be doing? Give the strike over to Miller, What does he do? Swings blindly to a ball on off and misses. A dot.

FOUR! But boundaries from Maharaj will surely hurt the Lankans. South Africa don't mind how they come as long as they come. Pin drop silence here in the stadium. Length ball around middle, Keshav swings, he only gets an inside edge past the diving keeper and into the fine leg fence.
A single now! Sri Lanka won't mind as they have Maharaj on strike. Length outside off, Miller guides it down to third man for a run.
On the pads, Miller clips it in the gap through the leg side and runs two. Good start to the over for South Africa.
Two dots to end another very good over by Perera. On a length around off, Maharaj goes for the cut but misses as the ball stays a touch low.
Bowls it around off, Maharaj tries to run it down but gets an inside edge towards the keeper.

NOT OUT! Maharaj is in. Excellent running by him. Miller punches it down towards long off and the batsmen complete one. Keshav wants a second and Miller obliges. They go for it. Shanaka at long off collects the ball and scores a direct hit at the bowler's end. The ball ricochets off the stumps as the batsmen run an overthrow. The umpire then signals for the third umpire and replays show Keshav to be safe. So three runs in total for the visitors and they need another 24.
Direct hit! Is Maharaj short of his crease? Well the Sri Lankans do not look confident.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. They pick up a single.
Another dot! Excellent by Perera. He bowls the leg cutter on a length. Maharaj tries to defend but gets beaten.
Miller batting sensibly here. He pushes this length ball around off and takes a run.
Powerplay 3 signaled! Now a total of 5 fielders can be placed outside the ring.

FOUR! Very costly! A boundary from the Free Hit and South Africa need 29 from 24. Poor from Lakmal too, he has all his fielders up on the off side and he bowls a half-volley outside off. Maharaj says thank you so much and goes over the fielders in the ring and fetches himself a boundary.
NO BALL! An extra fielder has been placed outside the ring as Miller pushes it towards mid off for a run. Free Hit coming up now. How costly will this prove?
Taps this towards covers and gets to the other end.
Keshav Maharaj comes out to bat.

OUT! A screamer by de Silva. Has that effort now tilted the game in Sri Lanka's favour? Well you can say so. Brilliant by him. Lakmal bowls a shorter delivery on middle, Mulder picks the length early and goes for the pull through mid-wicket. He though does not keep it down and Dhananjaya there dives full stretch to his left and takes it. Take a bow. In the first innings, de Kock did something similar to get rid of Mathews.
OHHHH! Close shave! Pressure now building here. Length ball outside off, Mulder goes after it with no foot movement. He gets an inside edge onto his pads.
WIDE! Poor from Lakmal, extras can't be bowled at this stage. Down the leg side, the batsman misses the flick and it has been wided.
A dot! Gold dust at the moment! Mulder steps down the track and Lakmal bowls it on his pads. He misses the flick and gets hit on the pads. 37 from 28.
Shortish on off, Miller punches it towards covers and gets to the other end. Sri Lanka won't mind this as Mulder will now be on strike.
Suranga Lakmal is brought back on.
Another delivery shorter in length on off, the batsman pushes it to the man at covers. Two dots to end a very good over by Perera.
Back of a length on off, Mulder punches it to covers.
Lovely comeback by Perera! On a length and it is the leg spinner. Mulder plays inside the line and gets beaten.

FOUR! What a shot to get off the mark. One would wonder after looking at that shot, why was he sent after Andile? Slightly short outside off, he guides it through backward point and the ball races to the fence. That should release the pressure which was building.
Willem Mulder strides out to the middle.

OUT! PLAYED ON! This was on the cards. South Africa are making a meal out of this now. Another cutter by Perera on middle, Phehlukwayo tries to work it on the leg side but gets an inside edge onto his pads and then onto his stumps. His struggle comes to an end. South Africa need another 42 from 34 deliveries.
Starts off with a cutter outside off, Miller pushes it through covers for a run.
Thisara Perera is back on.
Almost! Phehlukwayo dances down the track and de Silva spots that. He fires it outside off, AP somehow hits it towards covers. He too like Klaasen looks like getting out on any delivery.
On the pads again, Andile tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Clips it around the corner with the angle for a run. This is exactly what South Africa should be doing.
Flatter on off, AP goes back and tries to cut, he does so somehow as the ball was too close to play that shot. It goes through covers and a run results.
Fires this one short. Miller goes for the pull but the ball hurries onto him. He mistimes it towards long on. The keeper gets excited but there was no fielder there. A single taken.
Down the leg side and the umpire has wided it.
SIX! Miller gets into the action now. He says, enough of defending the deliveries. Uses his feet, gets to the pitch of the ball and hits it over the bowler's head for a biggie. 47 in 41 now.
Another swing and a miss! Not sure if this is needed here. Phehlukwayo makes room and tries to clear the off side but misses.
FOUR! In the air... but just wide! Another ball which is on the leg stump line, Andile flicks it in the air but away from the fielder at mid-wicket. Second boundary in the over.
Outside off, Andile looks to slash but misses. A hat-trick of dots...
Another dot. Full and straight, hit back towards the bowler who has a needless shy at the striker's end, missing them by a wide margin towards his left.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
FOUR! Bad start to the over. A short ball, around off, Phehlukwayo pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary!
Andile Phehlukwayo walks out to bat.

OUT! RUN OUT! Second wicket in the over and this is the only way Sri Lanka could have got Duminy tonight. Brilliant by Shanaka, can he do anything wrong in this game? Once again this was bowled flatter on off, JP punches it towards covers and sets off for a run. Shanaka gets to the ball quickly, picks it up, he has one stump to aim at and he hits bull's eye. Duminy continues running towards the dressing room as he knows he is well short. Sri Lanka start celebrating and the crowd here are ecstatic. Game on.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
On the stumps again, Miller plays a back foot defense.
Flatter and on off, Miller goes back and blocks it out.
David Miller walks out next.

OUT! So Klaasen who was desperately trying to get out, perishes courtesy an excellent catch by Mathews. De Silva gets his first. He fires it on the stumps, Klaasen makes room and once again tries to go over covers. He does not get the elevation though and it goes quickly to the left of Mathews. He moves swiftly and takes a tumbling catch. Throws the ball in the air in joy and Sri Lanka can still believe. 62 more needed.
Very full and on the pads, Duminy tries to flick but misses it get hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards short third man for a run.

Again, just out of the reach of the fielder. Luck too going South Africa's way. Just behind a length on middle, Klaasen goes for the pull but gets it nowhere off the middle. It goes high up in the air towards long on. Tharanga from mid on runs back but fails to reach it. Another brace.
A good yorker on middle, all Duminy can do is jam it out towards covers for a run.
Similar length to the last ball but offers width this time. HK slashes it through point for a single.
Back of a length, closer to the off pole. Klaasen keeps it out.

In the air... but falls just short. Good fielding in the end by the substitute Shehan Jayasuriya. Kumara bowls it full and outside off, Klaasen tries to go over covers but ends up slicing it towards sweeper cover. The fielder there runs to his left but fails to reach the ball. He though does well to stop it on the bounce. The batsmen run two.
Starts off with an expected shorter in length delivery, HK rocks back and defends it onto the ground.
Lahiru Kumara is back on.
Dropped short, pulled towards deep mid-wicket for one more.
Full on middle, pushed towards long on for another single.
Another cut shot, this time behind point for one.

FOUR! What a shot. Just a tad short, in line of the stumps, Klaasen picks it, takes it from the sticks and punches it through the covers. Had he missed it, he would have been cleaned up. Moves to 10 from 5 balls - 2 fours. The stand is worth 11 from 6 balls.
Punches this down to long off for a run.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.

FOUR! 'Oh yes!' screams an excited Mbangwa on air. Tossed up wide outside off, it is the leg spinner, Klaasen reads it, picks it and lofts it over wide mid off for a boundary! 79 more needed from 67 balls.
On middle, punched back to the bowler who misfields and parries it towards long on. Duminy wants a single but Klaasen asks him to stay where he is.
In comes the exciting Heinrich Klaasen.

OUT! Taken! Sri Lanka manage to get the breakthrough. Full and wide outside off, Amla looks to go hard at that, over the off side, but ends up slicing it. The result is a thick outside edge, not going where he intended to, but towards backward point instead where Lahiru Kumara does not drop it.Hashim falls 10 short of a half century but just get the feeling that this 57-run stand might have sealed the deal for the tourists.
The ball strikes the batsman very low on the pads. The batsmen have run through for a single. The umpire signals a leg bye.

SIX! THRASH! That is another terrific shot. Flighted on middle, Duminy jumps out of his crease and slogs it well over mid-wicket. 84 more needed from 71 balls. JP moves to 34 from 17 balls - 3 fours, 2 sixes.
WIDE. Full and outside leg, Duminy looks to sweep but misses. 50-RUN STAND IS UP, in just 26 balls.
Comes down the track and drives it towards long off for a single to raise the 100 FOR SOUTH AFRICA. Just 91 more needed from 72 balls.
Now Hashim comes down the track and bunts it over his partner towards long off for a single.
Full and outside leg, following Amla, driven back to the bowler.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.
WIDE. Darted down the leg side, Duminy tries to whip it fine but misses.
Full and around off, bunted through mid-wicket for a single.
Another change. Dhananjaya de Silva to bowl.
DROPPED! Lakmal is the culprit. Full and outside leg, Duminy looks to play the reverse sweep but cannot quite find the gap. Hits it straight to Suranga Lakmal at cover, who well, puts it down.
Full and around off, worked through mid-wicket for one.
Comes down the track and flicks it towards deep square leg for a run.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. One run added to the total.
FOUR! CARESSED! Tossed up outside off, Amla leans into this one and drives it through the covers for a boundary! The stand moves to 41 from 16 balls. 99 more needed from 82 balls.

'AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH'! A huge cry for a caught behind from Sri Lanka. The response? A signal for a wide from the umpire. Absolutely not interested. Sri Lanka do not even take the review. What a farce. Full and down the leg side, Amla looks to paddle but misses. The keeper first shouts for the catch, then the bowler joins but to no avail. Mathews starts to walk up for a chat regarding the review but is sent back by Dickwella.
Full and outside off, driven towards long off for a single.
Akila Dananjaya is back on.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total. 12 from that over, 30 from the last 2!
FOUR! And now he is being helped by some average bowling. A length ball, down the leg side, tickled towards the fine leg fence. 106 more needed from 85 balls.

FOUR! Wow. Has JP Duminy struck any ball better than in this innings? Pommie Mbangwa is testing all our cricket fans' memory by asking this question on air. I certainly don't remember. Tonight, he is playing with that air of 'I-am-invincible' confidence. Jumps down the track, converts the length ball into a half volley and boom. Crashes it through the covers for a boundary.
Full and outside off, Amla leans and drives it through the covers for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
A direct hit might have been interesting. Amla works this wide of mid-wicket and sets off for a quick single. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Replays are inconclusive.

FOUR LEG BYES! Down the leg side, Duminy tries to tick it fine but the ball goes off his pads past the keeper behind, to the fine leg fence. 18 from that over - the most expensive one of the innings! 117 more needed from 90 balls. The stand is already worth 23 from 8 balls.

A short ball outside leg, JP has no idea about that one, looks to fend it off as the ball kicks through the surface. He is not even watching the ball as it goes off the bat handle through square leg. The running is excellent as the batsmen return for the second.

SIX! TAKE THAT! Did we say everyone seems to be in a hurry? You bet, they are! A short ball, dropped around middle and leg, Duminy takes a couple of steps towards the bowler and pulls it with all his might. The contact is good enough and the ball sails over the mid-wicket fence! Moves to 12 from just 4 balls.
FOUR! Bad bowling. A short ball, outside leg, Duminy just pulls it through fine leg for a boundary. All the Protea batsmen seem to be in a hurry.
Outside off, steered towards third man for a run.
A short ball, pulled towards long leg for a single.
Another change. Lahiru Kumara into the attack.
FOUR! Well played, sir! A full toss, dipping on middle, Amla does not lose his mettle, just bends a bit and sweeps it, yes sweeps it past short fine leg for a boundary!
A short ball, around middle, helped wide of mid-wicket for a single to get off the mark.
JP Duminy walks in at number 4, replacing Hendricks.

OUT, DROPPED, CAUGHT! Taken on the rebound and the centurion in the last game departs cheaply in this one. Not the best of wicket-taking deliveries but Shanaka will not complain. A half volley outside off, Hendricks looks to drive this uppishly, over cover. However, he is unable to clear Dhananjaya de Silva at short extra cover who first stops the flow of the ball with his hand, then luckily for himself, sees the ball go up off his palms. Calmly takes it in the second attempt. Sri Lanka are jubilant. They need to keep picking up wickets. As far as Hendricks is concerned, well, that proverb goes for him - 'Everyday is not Sunday'... ahem...
A length ball now, a bit too straight, helped towards long leg for a run.
Outside off, Hendricks reaches out and pushes it behind point for a single. 50 UP FOR SOUTH AFRICA and we are just into the 5th over...
The batsman has played it to the point region. One run added to the total.
Dasun Shanaka introduced as well. Mathews ringing in the changes. Powerplay 2 signalled as well. 4 fielders allowed outside the circle till the 17th over.
Driven towards the mid on region. They pick up a single. 14 from that over, 27 in the last 2! South Africa end Powerplay 1 in style - 48/1.

FOUR! Excellent batting! Amla seems to be continuing from where he left off on Sunday. A length ball outside off again, this time Amla does not shuffle across. Albeit, he just whips it wide of mid on, in the air, towards long on for a boundary!

FOUR! Superb shot. Excellent wristwork. Not a bad ball at all. Thisara bowls it on a length close to the off stump and what does Amla do? Gets across and whips it efficiently past short fine leg for a boundary. 148 more needed from 104 balls.

Huge appeal for LBW but it is not given as it is BBW. Massive inside edge involved. Thisara bowls this on a length outside off, Hendricks looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. A quick single taken.
Full and outside off, Amla gets a long way across and clips it wide of mid on for a single.
WIDE. Shuffles across his sticks and Perera bowls it down the leg side. Amla misses his flick.
Full and too straight, clipped behind square on the leg side for a couple.
The hero of the previous game, Reeza Hendricks, walks out to bat. What can he do tonight? Meanwhile, Thisara Perera comes on to bowl as well. Amla will face him.

OUT! BOWLED 'EM! Lakmal has the last laugh. He gets a wicket on a full toss. He dishes out a high one. De Kock clears his front leg and tries to hit it through the off side but misses it completely and the ball hits the off pole. De Kock stands there in disbelief and then has a look at the umpire as he feels it is a no ball but the umpire has his hands down and de Kock has to walk back cheaply in his first outing as captain. A much-needed wicket for Sri Lanka. Can they now build on this?

Excellent batting this! Put away the good balls and respect the bad ones. That is exactly what the two batsmen are doing. On a length and around off, Amla taps it towards point and gets to the other end.
Clips it with the angle through the leg side and gets to the other end.

SIX! WOW! What a hit! Probably the shot of the game. De Kock makes room and Lakmal follows him but bowls it a touch too full. QDK shows the full face of the bat and lofts it over the bowler's head. The timing is such that it has carried all the way.
Once again the leg stump line, Amla this time works it through square leg and gets to the other end.
FOUR! Poor line to start with straightaway. Down the leg side and Amla is too good a batsman to miss out. He works it fine down the leg side and a boundary results.

Finally, we are now getting underway! Out come the umpires along with the Sri Lankan players. They are followed by the openers, Hashim Amla and Quinton de Kock. Suranga Lakmal will continue his spell. Here we go...

2155 local update - Hurrah! We are going to have a game after all! 21 overs allotted after all the reductions - target being 191. Who will be the happier side? Of course, if it does not rain... will we get a completed match?

2140 local update - Hmmm... well, good news... hopefully. The rain has stopped and the umpires are going to have an inspection in 15 minutes. But the catch is - play must start around 10 pm local. Just imagine... all the hard work down the drain for Sri Lanka if this is washed out. Fingers crossed...
2115 local - Good news! The rain has now stopped and the covers have been peeled off. Let us hope we have a resumption soon.

2045 local - Uh oh! Another break. It is more of a precautionary one as the umpires have looked at the ground staff who seem to be ready to take the covers on. Ohhh... as I type that, it is coming down heavily. And now as I typed that, it is almost gone! Hopefully, we should not have a big delay.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Good shot. On a length outside off, de Kock goes back and punches it through the covers.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.

In the air... safe! Hashim gets lucky now after de Kock in the previous over. He attempts anoter sweep but this time gets a top edge. Luckily for him, Suranga Lakmal, who was moved finer after the boundary, cannot get there. Had he been in the position as on the previous ball, he would have taken the catch with the ball landing around backward square leg. A single taken.

FOUR! Bad start. Full and outside leg, Amla gets down and paddles it past the man at short fine leg. 4000 ODI runs as a pair for Amla and de Kock - the first South African pair to do so and 11th overall.
Spin straightaway! Akila Dananjaya to bowl with the second new ball.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.
FOUR! The batsman works it down the leg side. The ball races to the boundary. The umpire signals four runs.
Full and straight, driven back to the bowler.

FOUR! Streaky! Lucky boundary for the skipper. On a length outside off, Quinton looks to punch it through the off side but is too far from the ball. Gets a thick inside edge which flies past the off stump. The Lankan keeper is moving to his left and hence is wrong-footed. The ball goes to his right and races to the fine leg fence. 4000 ODI runs for Quinton de Kock - the 12th Protea to achieve this feat and 6th fastest overall.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. They manage to come back for the second.
On a length outside off, de Kock looks to punch it through the off side but is too close to the ball and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.

What? They are back!!! Could not even prepare my coffee, let alone finish it. Sigh. But work comes first. The beverages can wait. Let us begin. Suranga Lakmal to Quinton de Kock will start off proceedings for this run chase. Hashim Amla is his partner. Here we go...
